tools.name: diagnose_crash
tools.description: Find the mod most likely behind a modded Minecraft crash (Fabric, NeoForge, Forge). Use it whenever the user shares a crash report or latest.log or says the game will not start. It is the only tool that reads logs, and it adds what the file does not hold: it checks every installed mod against the Mo

tools.name: search_mods
tools.description: Turn a mod's display name or part of its id into the exact mod id the other lab tools take, and see which mods the Modkeel lab has data on. Use it first when you only have a name ("Entity Culling", "Sodium") or are unsure of the id; skip it when you already have the id. Matching ignores case, spaces

tools.name: get_mod_info
tools.description: What one Minecraft mod is and where to get it: its Modrinth page (title, summary, categories, loaders, the Minecraft releases its author lists, client/server side, licence, downloads, source and issue links) next to a short Modkeel lab record (tested versions, run and pair counts). Use it for "what

tools.name: find_mod_download
tools.description: The exact file to install for one mod on one Minecraft version and loader, with its download link. Use it for "where do I get X for 1.21.1 Fabric?", after diagnose_crash names a mod that needs another build, or when updating a pack to a new version. Checks, best first: the author's own build on Modr

tools.name: get_mod_runs
tools.description: Everything the Modkeel lab saw one Minecraft mod do: each Minecraft version where it ran on a server or a client, or crashed, and every mod it ran with or clashed with. Use it for "does this mod work on 1.21.1?", "which versions was it tested on?" or to check a suspect from diagnose_crash. For one s

tools.name: check_mod_pair
tools.description: Whether two Minecraft mods ran together in the Modkeel lab, clashed, or were never tested together. Use it for "can I use X with Y?" or to check two suspects from diagnose_crash; for one mod's whole record, use get_mod_runs. Takes two mod ids in any order (from names, call search_mods first). tools.name: check_mod_list
tools.description: A whole mod list or modpack checked against the Modkeel lab at once: every pair in it that clashed, the mods whose jar crashed, the pairs that ran together, and the mods the lab has no data on. Use it for "will these mods work together?" or before updating a pack; for two mods, check_mod_pair is eno

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "diagnose_crash" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Find the mod most likely behind a modded Minecraft crash (Fabric, NeoForge, Forge). Pass the whole crash report (crash-reports/*.txt) or logs/latest.log as text. Returns the crash kind, the suspect mods ranked with reasons, how sure it is, and a fix guide. The text is read and dropped, not stored." → after: "Find the mod most likely behind a modded Minecraft crash (Fabric, NeoForge, Forge). Use it whenever the user shares a crash report or latest.log or says the game will not start. It is the only tool that reads logs, and it adds what the file does not hold: it checks every installed mod against the Mo"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
